mb0i7z: «Siempre que», «siempre y cuando», «con tal de que» and «a condición de que» present an essential condition: they are equivalent to «only if». With this meaning they always take the subjunctive. «A condición de que» is the most formal; «con tal de que» is common in conversation. If the subject is the same, you can use «con tal de» or «a condición de» + infinitive.
1vukubh: Be careful with «siempre que»: with the indicative it means «whenever» and sets no condition. «Siempre que llueve, se moja el pasillo» describes a habit; «les dejo la terraza siempre que la limpien» sets a condition. Agreement follows the week 2 rule: with a main verb in the past or conditional, the connector requires the imperfect subjunctive.
1t6os7j: The landlord said he would let us paint as long as we chose light colours.
pbqgjj: Whenever my sister comes, we sleep in the living room.
gc9ej1: As a necessary condition, «con tal de que» always takes the subjunctive.
1payica: «A no ser que», «a menos que», «salvo que» and «excepto que» introduce the only exception: they are equivalent to «unless». They also take the subjunctive. «Salvo que» with the indicative, on the other hand, means «except for the fact that» and presents a real fact: «the flat is perfect, except that the lift breaks down every week».
1fpf51n: «En caso de que» + subjunctive anticipates a possibility and says what to do if it happens; «por si» + indicative explains a precaution taken now. Finally, «como» + subjunctive at the start of a sentence is a colloquial warning or threat, often in jest; with the indicative, «como» is causal.
1we1ebs: In a formal text, avoid «como» + subjunctive: it sounds like a threat. Use «en caso de que» or «si».

1qx9coe: «Como si» compares what you see with an unreal or unconfirmed situation. It allows only two tenses: the imperfect subjunctive if the imagined thing happens at the same time («Nico habla como si fuera el dueño») and the pluperfect if it is earlier («entró como si no hubiera pasado nada»). The tense of the main verb does not change this choice: he talks, talked or will talk «como si fuera el dueño».
4yp206: After «como si» there is never a present subjunctive, indicative or conditional. For a real, known manner «como» + indicative is used («hazlo como te expliqué»). And to protest in a colloquial tone there is «¡ni que…!»: «¡Ni que fuera tu empleada!» means «you are behaving as if I were, but I'm not».

17550k7: Information guide from a university office
1ohtfjy: Original SpanishCue text written as a guide from the accommodation office of a fictional university in Córdoba. The cases and names are invented; it is not legal advice.
wc50ua: Every March, thousands of students arrive in Córdoba and share a flat for the first time. The experience is usually good, as long as some basic rules are followed from the start. This guide brings together the most frequent questions we received last year and some real cases, with the names changed.
1d2o7z6: Before signing, read the whole contract. Many landlords accept students without a guarantor on condition that they pay a two-month deposit. Don't sign unless the contract states when and how that money will be returned. If the flat has prior damage, take photos of it on the first day and send them to the landlord in writing. Lucas, a medical student, wrote to us in November: «If I had taken photos of the stain on the ceiling, they wouldn't have deducted half my deposit». Just in case you ever need them, keep all the receipts too.
1tz2shw: Living together requires explicit agreements. We recommend that, during the first week, each group writes a chore rota and decides how it will split the costs. Rules work best if nobody imposes them: when one person runs the house as if they were the owner, the others stop feeling that the rules are theirs. An exchange student told us that her flatmate behaved as if he had lived there all his life and she had just arrived on a visit. She felt like a guest in her own home.
rwjbqk: Money deserves a section of its own. The fairest approach is to split fixed costs equally, unless someone has a much bigger room; in that case, they can pay a little more. Open a shared account or a shared spreadsheet in the first week, in case questions come up later. A student from Jujuy told us that, for months, her flatmate paid the electricity late as if the bills arrived by themselves. «If only I had said something in April», she wrote to us. «If I had, they wouldn't have cut off the service in the middle of winter».
1gwyeon: The most common conflicts have to do with noise, cleaning and visitors. Whenever there's a problem, it's best to talk about it in person and soon. A third-year group explained their method to us: anyone can invite someone to stay the night, as long as they give a day's notice and it isn't more than twice a week. «If we had agreed on it from March», one of them admitted, «we wouldn't be so tired of arguing today».
1kfcaig: Finally, think about leaving right from the moment you move in. If a student has to leave before the contract ends, they can usually do so by giving a month's notice, unless the contract says otherwise. Our office checks contracts free of charge: if people had brought them to us earlier, many of the cases in this guide would never have happened. Book an appointment; there's no need to wait until there is a problem.
